dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: This little one has recovered well, thanks to your diligent care. When I return, I'll ask around in advance.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: If fortune smiles on me and I manage to locate its herd, then the next time I come, it will be to send this fawn home.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I understand. You cannot bear to see it leave. But this little Rimehorn Deer has its own family, and its father, mother, and friends must surely be worried sick.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Once it is well, I believe it would be best to have it reunite with its own.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: I know! But it's... it's not well yet...

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Does your leg still hurt? Do you... Do you wanna go home?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: It says, "It doesn't hurt anymore. But can you brush my fur again?"

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Okay! Let me grab my comb, I just asked Ineffa to make a new one yesterday!

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: If you like it, you can take it back with you. To your family.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: ...Wait, huh? Where'd I put it? Lemme go back home and dig around.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Then I shall take my leave. Once again, I thank you for taking such good care of the little one. I came in a rush today, so next time, I shall prepare some gifts.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Do not force yourself to go out of your way for gifts, Miss Lauma. Aino loves the deer, and I do too. It is only natural for us to care for it.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Besides, Aino and I are happy to have the chance to talk to it.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Is that so? Haha, well, the Rimehorn Deer is very fond of you too. I'm sure it considers both of you its true friends.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I believe this is a friendship that will not fade, even if you are worlds apart.
